# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-4293

# Review — PAN-4293
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` makes browsers send `Origin: null`, so every real-browser POST to `/activate`, `/activate/confirm` and `/admin/*` is refused with 403

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4293-review-bfce58ab
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4293/.pan/review/agent-pan-4293-review-bfce58ab/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4293 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4293
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/4483 (headRefOid = reviewed HEAD)
- HEAD reviewed: bfce58abac3bf5d563b534dcd7229fb249561818
- Base / prior cycle SHA: prior cycle reviewed c9c4ca3f5ce (run agent-pan-4293-review-c9c4ca3f, CHANGES REQUESTED). Since then:
  - fb8b2a59050 is the fix commit.
  - 5cabe339e17 is plan state only.
  - bfce58abac3 merges origin/main (PAN-4455, #4472).
  - The main merge touches no `services/account`, `tests/**/services/account` or `docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md` file. The only account-service delta is fb8b2a59050.

## Prior findings: verification

| Prior finding | Status at bfce58ab |
| --- | --- |
| Blocker: no Origin/CSRF check on `POST /activate/confirm` | Cross-site posts are now refused (`device-flow.ts`, `sameOrigin`, on `activateSubmit` and `activateConfirm`), with unit and Miniflare tests. **But the check also refuses legitimate browser posts. See the new blocker below.** |
| `~` URIError from `matchPattern` | Fixed: `routes.ts` catches the decode and returns `null`, giving 404; test added in `routes.test.ts` |
| `~` `activate-fail` counted after lookup | Fixed: `peek()` (`rate-limit.ts`) refuses before any lookup once `count >= limit`, so the 11th request after 10 wrong codes gets 429; test added |
| `?` Read-then-delete of approved device grants | Fixed: `DELETE … WHERE status = 'approved' RETURNING *` consumes the grant atomically; concurrent-poll test added |
| `?` Deleting non-owner leaves a pending row | Fixed: `resolveSignIn` checks `users.deleted_at` by `github_id` before the allowlist gate |
| `≉` Admin header shows id, not login | Declined with a reason (no login is stored for the owner). Accepted as cosmetic |
| `?` Re-adding resets `granted_at` | Declined as intended. Accepted |

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] Browsers send `Origin: null` under `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, so the device flow and the admin screen refuse their own forms — `services/account/src/http.ts:22`
- Severity: `!` MUST. FR-2 (the device flow approves in a browser) and FR-8, FR-9 and FR-10 (the owner signs in and manages grants) fail in a real browser.
- Classification / requirement scope: **specification defect** (two PRD decisions contradict each other); in_pr_scope.
  - D-28 requires every HTML response to carry `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
  - D-20 requires every admin POST to carry "an `Origin` header equal to the origin of `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`".
  - fb8b2a59050 applied the same equality check to `/activate`, following my cycle-1 recommendation.
  - The Fetch Standard ("append a request `Origin` header") says: when a request's method is neither GET nor HEAD and its mode is not "cors", a referrer policy of `no-referrer` sets the serialized Origin to `null`. A form submission from a page served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` therefore sends `Origin: null`, which never equals `https://account.overdeck.ai`.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: every HTML page comes from `html()` with `HTML_HEADERS` (`http.ts:18-23`). Each form on those pages POSTs to a handler that compares `Origin` for equality:
  - The confirm page posts to `/activate/confirm` (`device-flow.ts`, `activateConfirm`).
  - The activate form posts to `/activate` (`activateSubmit`).
  - The admin sign-in page posts to `/admin/login` (`admin/session.ts:54`).
  - Every admin form (add, revoke, allow, logout) goes through `requireOwnerSession` (`admin/session.ts:98`).
- Expected / observed / impact:
  - Expected: a person who opens `/activate`, enters the code and clicks Continue reaches GitHub. The owner who clicks "Sign in with GitHub" on `/admin` reaches GitHub.
  - Observed: both get the 403 "Request rejected" page.
  - Impact: the device flow cannot complete in a browser (the CLI, SSH and headless sign-in path). The admin screen cannot be signed into at all, so no tester can be added or allowed. The PKCE flow is unaffected (GET only).
- Evidence (runtime, real browser):
  - Setup: a scratchpad probe served the PR's own `handle()` (through the unit harness, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) behind a Node HTTP server. Playwright Chromium then loaded `/activate?user_code=<real code>`, clicked Continue, loaded `/admin` and clicked "Sign in with GitHub".
  - Result:
    ```
    /activate Origin="null"         chromium /activate -> 403
    /admin/login Origin="null"      chromium /admin/login -> 403
    ```
  - Control: the same run with only the `Referrer-Policy` response header stripped.
    ```
    /activate Origin="http://127.0.0.1:38918"      chromium /activate -> 200
    /admin/login Origin="http://127.0.0.1:38918"   chromium /admin/login -> 302
    ```
  - Limits: Chromium only; the installed Playwright Firefox build was missing. Firefox follows the same Fetch Standard step. The probe used `http://127.0.0.1` rather than https, but the `no-referrer` → `null` rule does not depend on scheme.
  - Why the unit and Miniflare tests pass: the harness sets `Origin` explicitly (`tests/unit/services/account/helpers/admin.ts:31`, and the Miniflare device scenario). No test exercises a browser's own Origin serialization.
- Why the earlier review missed it: cycle 1 checked the Origin comparison only against cross-site requests and the test harness. It did not trace how the page's own `Referrer-Policy` changes the Origin a browser sends. The admin half has been present since the admin-session work item and c9c4ca3f; the activate half came from my cycle-1 fix recommendation. Both are reported now.
- Fix: change the HTML `Referrer-Policy` to `same-origin`.
  - Same-origin form posts then carry the real `Origin`.
  - Cross-site posts still differ from `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and stay refused. Under `same-origin`, a cross-origin form gets either its own origin or `null`, and both fail the check.
  - Outbound navigations to github.com still send no `Referer`.
  - Do not loosen the checks to accept `null`; that would reopen the cycle-1 CSRF hole on `/activate/confirm`.
  - Add a regression guard. The minimum is a `routes.test.ts` assertion that HTML responses carry `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`, with a comment naming the Origin dependency. A real-browser check is better if the project accepts a Playwright test here.
  - Spec correction: amend D-28 to `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` and state why. Update the `docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md` "API" header sentence to match.

## Non-blocking Findings
None new. The two declined cosmetic items from cycle 1 are accepted as reasoned.

## Coverage

### Changed-file ledger
- All 58 files were reviewed in cycle 1 at c9c4ca3f (ledger in `.pan/review/agent-pan-4293-review-c9c4ca3f/review.md`).
- This cycle re-reviewed every account-service file fb8b2a59050 changed: `device-flow.ts`, `rate-limit.ts`, `routes.ts`, `sign-in.ts`, `docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md`, `miniflare.test.ts`, `device-flow.test.ts`, `github-callback.test.ts`, `rate-limit.test.ts` and `routes.test.ts`.
- It also re-read `http.ts` and `admin/session.ts` for the new blocker.
- The `.pan/continues/PAN-4293.xbrief.json` change is plan state only and is not applicable to runtime.
- The main-merge files (PAN-4455: frontend, `configuration/*.mdx`, `docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md`, `docs/SESSION-VAULT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json` line, `.overdeck/context/codebase/conventions.md`, PAN-4455 plan files) come from main and are outside this issue's diff against main.

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** fixes verified as above. New blocker found.
- **Security:** the cross-site refusal holds. The recommended fix keeps it, because the Origin check stays strict.
- **Performance:**
  - `peek()` adds one indexed SELECT per `POST /activate`.
  - The `resolveSignIn` deleted-account check adds one SELECT on the `users.github_id` unique index per sign-in.
  - Both are negligible.
- **Requirements/UX:** FR-2 and FR-8, FR-9 and FR-10 fail end to end in a real browser (the blocker). AC-1 to AC-18 are otherwise as recorded in cycle 1.

### Acceptance criteria (deltas from cycle 1)
| AC | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-8 (device flow) | Unverified for this HEAD; the tests pass only with an injected Origin | Real-browser probe: `/activate` → 403 |
| AC-12/13/14 (admin) | Unverified for this HEAD; the tests pass only with an injected Origin | Real-browser probe: `/admin/login` → 403 |
| AC-15 (Miniflare) | Unverified for this HEAD | CI test shards were still pending at review time |
| Others | As in cycle 1 | No account-service change besides fb8b2a59050 |

## Verification
- CI for bfce58ab (`gh pr checks 4483`): test-shard 1–4/4, test-e2e, build and the lint-groups were **pending** at review time. Only the clean-install smoke test, the prompt-trailer gate and CodeRabbit had passed. Test results for this HEAD are unverified.
- `npm run lint:effect-diagnostics`: no Effect or `src/` change in the account-service delta, so not applicable. The `lint-group (effect)` job for this HEAD was pending.
- Probes (scratchpad only; no tracked file was edited): Playwright Chromium against `handle()` behind a local HTTP server, with and without `Referrer-Policy` (output above).
- I did not run the full suite or deploy anything.
